changing room = a room where players change clothes before and after sport
dugout = the shelter beside the pitch where the coach and substitutes sit
grandstand = the main, often covered, stand with the best seats
floodlights = powerful lights that allow sport to be played after dark
sports venue = a place designed for sport, such as a stadium, pool or hall
gym = a place with equipment for physical training
racket = the strung implement used to hit the ball or shuttlecock
helmet = a hard hat that protects the head in cycling, skating or riding
shin pads = guards worn on the lower legs, especially in football
gumshield = a plastic guard worn in the mouth to protect the teeth
goggles = protective glasses for swimming, skiing or cycling
wetsuit = a close-fitting rubber suit that keeps you warm in cold water
trainers = comfortable sports shoes for running or the gym
football boots = studded shoes designed for football or rugby on grass
spikes = running shoes with metal points for grip on a track
stopwatch = a watch used to measure exact times in training or races
scoreboard = a board that displays the score and sometimes the time
goalposts = the two upright posts, and usually a bar, that form a goal
shuttlecock = the feathered or plastic object hit in badminton
puck = the hard rubber disc used in ice hockey
